correction.text: "an Epipalaeolithic tradition in Algeria and Tunisia"; "named after the town of Gafsa, Tunisia (Capsa in Latin)"; Tunisia and the part of Algeria north of 33.5 N and east of 3 E (western Algeria and Morocco are left out, the Sahara part too)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. "The Capsian was an Epipalaeolithic tradition in Algeria and Tunisia from ca. 9000 to 5400 cal BC." Tunisia plus Algeria north of 33.5 N and east of 3 E (1,204 land cells, about 304,612 km2) is the dossier's placement: the first page names only the two countries, the type town Gafsa and "the environment of the Maghreb" as open savanna, and has no infobox, site count or area; the Iberomaurusian page (second page) says the Capsian is found "In Algeria, Tunisia, and Libya, but not in Morocco" and that "In Morocco and western Algeria, the Iberomaurusian is succeeded by the Cardial culture after a long hiatus", which is why western Algeria is left out. Taking all of Algeria (8,798 cells) would put the culture over the Sahara; Libya is not drawn (see notes).

ledger.note: 6000 BCE (project floor): the Capsian still holds Tunisia and eastern Algeria. "The Capsian was an Epipalaeolithic tradition in Algeria and Tunisia from ca. 9000 to 5400 cal BC." The tradition begins about 3,000 years before the floor; the countries are the page's, the 33.5 N and 3 E cuts are the dossier's, informed by the Iberomaurusian page.

ledger.note: 5400 BCE: the Capsian ends. "from ca. 9000 to 5400 cal BC"; "During the succeeding Neolithic of Capsian Tradition, there is evidence from one site" of domesticated ovicaprids, which the page gives no dates or extent for, so the land passes to nobody and the Neolithic of Capsian Tradition is kept in the notes.

certainty.note: A tradition known from sites; no border is recorded.

notes: Capsian culture, Tunisia and Algeria. One page. The page cites a reference title "The Capsian (10,000-6000 B.P.)" (8050-4050 BCE) against its own "ca. 9000 to 5400 cal BC"; the page's sentence is used. The Neolithic of Capsian Tradition that "succeeds" it has no dates on the page and no dossier; the Maghreb after 5400 BCE is blank. The Iberomaurusian (earlier, map caption on the page) is not dated on the page and is not drawn. Morocco is outside the drawn extent. Second page (Iberomaurusian, opened 2026-10-18): infobox "Followed by: Mushabian, Cardium pottery, Capsian"; the Capsian "believed either to have spread into north Africa from the Near East or to have evolved from the Iberomaurusian"; "In Algeria, Tunisia, and Libya, but not in Morocco". Libya is named there but with no site or date; the Libyan Sahara is carried by green-sahara-cultures. Farming arrives in north-west Africa "around 5,500 BCE" (Cardial) and pastoralists "around 5000 BCE", both after the Capsian region as drawn is cut.
